messages.re: connecting slave requested to start from GTID [\d-]+, which is not in the master's binlog

statement_timeout: EXPLAIN <your query>;  -- look for type = ALL and a big rows number
-- MariaDB's limit is max_statement_time (seconds); add the missing index rather than raising it.
check_violation: SELECT CHECK_CLAUSE FROM information_schema.CHECK_CONSTRAINTS WHERE CONSTRAINT_NAME = '{constraint}';
lock_wait: -- If a forgotten transaction blocks: KILL <trx_mysql_thread_id>;  (after checking what it is)
write_on_replica: SELECT @@hostname, @@port, @@read_only;   -- read_only = 1: this server is a replica or switched to read-only (MariaDB has no super_read_only; users with READ ONLY ADMIN can still write)
-- Send writes to the primary: check the host in the app's database config. After a failover, recycle the app's connection pool.
-- Common mistake: SET GLOBAL read_only = OFF on a replica to make the error go away; writes there make it drift and stop replication later.

sql: SELECT variable_value FROM information_schema.global_status WHERE variable_name = 'MAX_USED_CONNECTIONS'

binlog_not_expiring.sql: SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES v WHERE v.VARIABLE_NAME = 'LOG_BIN' AND v.VARIABLE_VALUE = 'ON' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.GLOBAL_VARIABLES e WHERE e.VARIABLE_NAME IN ('BINLOG_EXPIRE_LOGS_SECONDS', 'EXPIRE_LOGS_DAYS', 'MAX_BINLOG_TOTAL_SIZE') AND e.VARIABLE_VALUE + 0 > 0)
binlog_not_expiring.proof: binary logging is on and no expiry or size limit is set, so old binary logs are never removed
